limits: Exod. 6:2-3 is quoted as in LXX. Justin uses the passage to show one who appears and speaks is God; he does not argue a second 'name'.

ref: Dial. 127 (chapter as in PG 6 and ANF; no section numbers in sources)
greek: Ὁ γὰρ ἄῤῥητος Πατὴρ καὶ κύριος τῶν πάντων οὔτε ποι ἀφῖκται, οὔτε περιπατεῖ, οὔτε καθεύδει, οὔτε ἀνίσταται, ἀλλ᾽ ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ χώρᾳ, ὅπου ποτὲ, μένει, ὀξὺ ὁρῶν, καὶ ὀξὺ ἀκούων, οὐκ ὀφθαλμοῖς οὐδὲ ὠσὶν, ἀλλὰ δυνάμει ἀλέκτῳ· καὶ πάντα ἐφορᾷ, καὶ πάντα γινώσκει· οὔτε κινούμενος ὁ τόπῳ τε ἀχώρητος, καὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ὅλῳ, ὅς γε ἦν καὶ πρὶν τὸν κόσμον γενέσθαι.

english: For the ineffable Father and Lord of all neither has come to any place, nor walks, nor sleeps, nor rises up, but remains in His own place, wherever that is, quick to behold and quick to hear, having neither eyes nor ears, but being of indescribable might; and He sees all things, and knows all things, and He is not moved or confined to a spot in the whole world, for He existed before the world was made.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; CCEL introductory note: 'Messrs. Dods and Reith')

what_it_says: The ineffable Father does not move, and is not in any place; he is seen only through the Son/angel.

limits: Gives the 'ineffable, not in any place' that the brief asked for. Opponents will say it sets the Father far from the Logos. The Greek has two OCR doubts: 'ὁ τόπῳ' (probably ἢ τόπῳ) and 'ἀλέκτῳ' (probably ἀληκτῳ); flagged, not corrected.

what_it_says: The one seen was the Son, who is God, sent 'according to his will' (κατὰ βουλήν), an Angel serving the Father's will (γνώμη); he was willed to be born of the Virgin.

limits: This is the passage for the brief's 'in boulesei / in gnome' point: βουλή and γνώμη are both used. The '[saw]' is the translator's. Note '(21)' is an OCR apparatus marker. Justin does not say the Son's will differs from the Father's here.

greek: Οὔτε οὖν Ἀβραὰμ, οὔτε Ἰσαὰκ, οὔτε Ἰακὼβ, οὔτε ἄλλος ἀνθρώπων εἶδε τὸν Πατέρα καὶ ἄῤῥητον Κύριον τῶν πάντων ἁπλῶς, καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ.

english: Therefore neither Abraham, nor Isaac, nor Jacob, nor any other man, saw the Father and ineffable Lord of all, and also of Christ.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; CCEL introductory note: 'Messrs. Dods and Reith')

what_it_says: No patriarch saw the Father; they saw the Son, the one who is God and angel.
use: supports Trinitarian reading (the Son is the visible one; the Father is never seen)
limits: The Father is 'ineffable Lord of all'; 'Christ' is named with the Father in the same clause, which Justin uses to distinguish them. This is a claim about theophanies, not about the Spirit.
